description: Several independently quotable thoughts in one passage, expressing substantially different ideas, none of which should be merged or treated as duplicates.
sourceText: Courage is not the absence of fear but the decision that something else matters more than fear. Wisdom, unlike knowledge, cannot be transferred from one mind to another through mere instruction. A person who never fails has simply never attempted anything worth the risk. Friendship, when genuine, survives disagreement precisely because it was never built on agreement in the first place. These four observations, though related in spirit, stand on their own and were developed independently across many years of reflection and conversation with colleagues and students alike.
